messages.subject: [Rd] rchk on github
messages.body_plain:
I'm noticing that some CRAN infrastructure still seems to be hosted 
on Tomas Kalibera's github account, which will presumably go away at 
some point ...

https://github.com/kalibera/rchk

There are a few up-to-date forks lying around (just forked it myself), 
so I guess the content can be rescued even if this repo suddenly goes 
away ... ??

   A similar question goes for his dockerhub images: 
https://hub.docker.com/u/kalibera (maybe the rocker project would take 
those over ... ??)

   cheers
     Ben Bolker

messages.subject: [Rd] request for use cases for larger integers in R
messages.subject_clean: request for use cases for larger integers in R
messages.body_plain:
I just joined the listserv so apologies if this is not threaded in the original discussion
https://stat.ethz.ch/pipermail/r-devel/2026-July/084631.html

A restating of the use cases from Kevin Ushey:
 1. Language interop - C/C++/Fortran, Python via reticulate, Java via rJava, Javascript / JSON APIs
 2. Data structure interop - arrow, DBI (BIGINT), parquet, hdf5, zarr
There are use cases in both single-cell / spatial transcriptomics - big sparse array where we need interop above or the ability to handle more than 2^53-1.

messages.subject_clean: request for use cases for larger integers in R
messages.body_plain:
Going back even earlier, back in 2011 when I was at Google we funded some
work on bringing 64-bit integers into R:

  https://opensource.googleblog.com/2011/11/bringing-64-bit-data-to-r.html

Some of the use cases were language interop, differentiating between 64-bit
quantities used as identifiers efficiently, etc.

Around that time I also submitted a patch we had for a few releases of R to
prevent 2^53 == 2^53 + 1 from returning TRUE which was unfortunately backed
out of a later release of R.

        - Murray
